title: VisionReasoner: Unified Reasoning-Integrated Visual Perception via Reinforcement Learning
claim: One unified model handles many perception tasks with explicit reasoning and beats its baselines across diverse benchmarks without losing general abilities.
layout: 3 panels: top example rows by task, bottom radar chart and bar chart
description: The figure has three panels. Panel (a), the top and largest, is a dashed box split into three rows for Detection, Segmentation and Counting. Each row has a navy task label with a text query on the left, then the input photo, then a <think> reasoning paragraph with key phrases in blue italics. On the right is the output photo: a green box on the Statue of Liberty, red-highlighted tents, and numbered red boats totaling 8. Panel (b), bottom left, is a radar chart over seven benchmarks (COCO, RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg, ReasonSeg, CountBench, PixmoCount). A larger blue polygon for the proposed model encloses smaller teal and grey polygons. Panel (c), bottom right, is a grouped bar chart over seven VQA benchmarks. Grey, teal and navy bars compare Qwen2VL, Qwen2.5VL and the proposed model, which is roughly on par. The eye goes first to the photo rows.
caption: (a) VisionReasoner addresses diverse tasks within a unified framework. It generates a reasoning process and outputs the expected result corresponding to each query. (b) VisionReasoner significantly outperforms Qwen2.5VL. (c) VisionReasoner retains strong VQA capabilities.
abstract: Large vision-language models exhibit inherent capabilities to handle diverse visual perception tasks. In this paper, we introduce VisionReasoner, a unified framework capable of reasoning and solving multiple visual perception tasks within a shared model. Specifically, by designing a unified reward mechanism and multi-object cognitive learning strategies, VisionReasoner enhances its reasoning capabilities to analyze visual inputs, and addresses diverse perception tasks within a unified model. VisionReasoner generates a structured reasoning process before delivering the desired outputs responding to user queries. Human evaluation reveals the reasoning process of VisionReasoner is faithful and reliable even without annotated reasoning train data. To rigorously assess unified visual perception capabilities, we evaluate VisionReasoner on ten diverse tasks spanning three critical domains: detection, segmentation, and counting. Experimental results show that VisionReasoner achieves superior performance as a unified model, outperforming the baseline Qwen2.5VL by relative margins of 29.1\% on COCO (detection), 22.1\% on ReasonSeg (segmentation), and 13.2\% on CountBench (counting).
